headline: Trump administration pauses visa appointments worldwide
summary: The US State Department has suspended services to launch a global training initiative for consular officers to screen applicants more strictly.
details: The Donald Trump administration has issued a global pause on visa appointments, as part of an ongoing immigration crackdown in his second term.
A US State Department spokesperson stated that the pause is to accommodate a global training initiative for consular officers at all US embassies and consulates worldwide.
The training aims to help officers better screen out applicants who are likely to become dependent on US public benefits and ensure evaluations are consistent.
Immigrant visa applicants with already scheduled interviews have been notified via email that their appointments are being rescheduled.
This move comes amid a broader crackdown that includes the revocation of visas and green cards for reasons such as political opinions and pro-Palestinian protests.
Human rights groups have condemned these actions as discriminatory and in violation of free speech and due process rights.
While the administration focuses on stopping illegal immigration, it has also made legal immigration more difficult by imposing new and expensive fees for certain work visas.
The crackdown has faced some legal challenges, with a US judge recently striking down a policy that suspended immigrant visas for applicants from 75 countries.
caption:
US visa appointments are paused worldwide. The Trump administration is retraining consular officers to screen applicants more strictly.

The Donald Trump administration has issued a global pause on visa appointments, as part of an ongoing immigration crackdown in his second term.

A US State Department spokesperson stated that the pause is to accommodate a global training initiative for consular officers at all US embassies and consulates worldwide.

The training aims to help officers better screen out applicants who are likely to become dependent on US public benefits and ensure evaluations are consistent.

Immigrant visa applicants with already scheduled interviews have been notified via email that their appointments are being rescheduled.

This move comes amid a broader crackdown that includes the revocation of visas and green cards for reasons such as political opinions and pro-Palestinian protests.

Human rights groups have condemned these actions as discriminatory and in violation of free speech and due process rights.

While the administration focuses on stopping illegal immigration, it has also made legal immigration more difficult by imposing new and expensive fees for certain work visas.

The crackdown has faced some legal challenges, with a US judge recently striking down a policy that suspended immigrant visas for applicants from 75 countries.

headline: Man arrested after ex-wife's hand almost severed in Meherpur attack
summary: The suspect, identified as Shawon, allegedly hacked his former wife and her parents at their home in the early hours of the morning.
details: A man has been arrested in Meherpur after allegedly attacking his former wife and her parents with a sharp weapon at their home.
The suspect, Shawon, reportedly entered the house in the Lord Market area around 1:30 am and attacked his ex-wife, Smriti.
When Smriti's parents rushed to help her, Shawon allegedly hacked them as well, leaving both injured.
According to the resident medical officer at Meherpur General Hospital, Smriti's hand was almost severed from the wrist, while her parents suffered various injuries.
The three victims have been referred to Dhaka for more advanced treatment.
Police stated that the couple had previously been divorced due to marital disputes.
Shawon was arrested by police during a raid conducted around 7:00 am the following morning.
